nodes.description: Immutable reference to the Ponzi game contract at 0xEB82AE50FA5b15FFc2699143b3da1B524127853B, queried by yield() via the Ponzi interface.
mapping(address => uint256) recording the last block.timestamp at which each address claimed yield; used as the 24h cooldown guard.
Inherited ERC20 private total supply, increased by _mint on every yield claim.
Constructor(uint256 initialSupply) initialises ERC20Detailed metadata and mints the whole initial supply to msg.sender.
Public, permissionless yield() function: enforces a 24h cooldown via lastTime, reads the caller's Ponzi player record, computes an unbounded payout and mints it.
Inherited internal mint function that creates tokens, increases _totalSupply and credits _balances[account]; called by constructor and yield.
Public ERC20 transfer using _msgSender() as the sender; part of the inherited token surface.
Public ERC20 transferFrom using _msgSender() as the spender whose allowance is consumed.
Caller-controlled address; used as the yield claimant, cooldown key, Ponzi player lookup key, mint recipient and ERC20 sender/spender.
Miner-adjustable timestamp used for the 24h cooldown check and directly inside the payout arithmetic.
External call ponzi.players(msg.sender) on a hard-coded contract; return values (id, deposit, regTime) are implicitly trusted and not validated for freshness or sanity.
Unchecked raw multiplication deposit * (block.timestamp - regTime) in Solidity 0.6.4 without SafeMath, allowing integer overflow of the computed payout value.
Permissionless _mint(msg.sender, payout) in yield(): any address that ever registered as a Ponzi player can inflate the token supply once per 24h with no owner/role check.
Constructor parameter controlling the initial token supply minted to the deployer.
Player id returned by the ponzi.players external call; unused afterwards.
Player deposit amount returned by ponzi.players; multiplied by elapsed time to derive the payout.
Player registration time returned by ponzi.players; used both as a non-participation guard and as the payout time base.
Locally computed mint amount = deposit * (block.timestamp - regTime); fully attacker-influenced and unbounded.

edges.reason: msg.sender is the caller of yield() and keys the lastTime mapping lookup.
block.timestamp gates the 24h cooldown require in yield().
initialSupply parameter flows into the constructor mint.
Constructor invokes _mint to create the initial supply.
msg.sender is the mint recipient in both constructor and yield().
lastTime[msg.sender] is overwritten with block.timestamp as the cooldown marker.
lastTime is read in the require that implements the 24h timestamp-dependent access rule.
yield() performs the external ponzi.players call.
msg.sender is passed as the player argument to ponzi.players.
External call returns id into local variable id.
External call returns deposit into local variable deposit.
External call returns regTime into local variable regTime.
block.timestamp directly feeds the payout multiplication, enabling timestamp manipulation of minted amount.
deposit is the left operand of the unchecked payout multiplication.
regTime is subtracted from block.timestamp inside the payout computation.
Unchecked raw multiplication result is assigned to payout in Solidity 0.6.4, so it can overflow silently.
The attacker-influenced, unbounded payout value is minted as new tokens.
yield() executes the _mint(msg.sender, payout) operation.
Any msg.sender satisfying the cooldown and player check can mint tokens to itself; no privileged role is required.
The unchecked mint in yield() forwards into ERC20._mint.
Repeated permissionless mints inflate _totalSupply without any supply cap.
The external call to the hard-coded ponzi contract executes arbitrary external code before _mint completes, creating a reentrancy surface into yield().
transfer() uses _msgSender() (msg.sender) as the debited account.
transferFrom() uses _msgSender() (msg.sender) as the spender whose allowance is consumed.

normalization_plan.reason: The initial supply parameter only exists to feed the constructor mint call and carries no independent security semantics.
id is a purely local by-product of the ponzi.players external call and is never used, so it collapses into that call node.
deposit is only consumed as an operand of the unchecked payout multiplication.
regTime is only consumed as the subtracted time base of the unchecked payout multiplication.
payout is a transient local whose sole purpose is to carry the computed value into the unchecked mint sink.
